newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-YANKEES NIP MARINERS, MARTINEZ ENDS APRIL WITH 35 RBI.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-YANKEES NIP MARINERS, MARTINEZ ENDS APRIL WITH 35 RBI.

text.p: David Wells allowed one run over 7-2/3 innings, and Tino Martinez capped a spectacular April with his ninth homer as the New York Yankees edged the Seattle Mariners 3-2 on Wednesday.
Wells (2-1) allowed seven hits, walked none and struck out a season-high nine batters.
"Everything was working, I stayed down in the zone, I had a good changeup, I was just bearing down and pitching," Wells said.
Martinez had two hits and added another RBI to his major-league record, finishing the month with 35.

In Boston, Chris Hammond allowed one run over five innings for his first American League win and Nomar Garciaparra had three hits and scored four times to lead the Boston Red Sox to an 11-2 rout of the Anaheim Angels.
Hammond, making his second start after eight relief appearances this year, gave up five hits and two walks with three strikeouts.
Mo Vaughn, Reggie Jefferson and Tim Naehring each drove in two runs for Boston, which had lost three of its last four games.

In Chicago, Mike Simms hit his first grand slam and Bobby Witt came on for an injured Ken Hill and became the American League's second five-game winner as the Texas Rangers beat the Chicago White Sox 6-2 in a game shortened to 6-1/2 innings by rain.
Hill pitched 1-1/3 innings before leaving with a strained right rotator cuff.
Witt (5-0), the third Texas pitcher, worked two scoreless innings and joined Andy Pettitte of the New York Yankees as the AL's only five-game winners.
The game was called after a 40-minute rain delay in the top of the seventh inning with nobody out and the tying run on deck.
In Cleveland, Mark McGwire and Geronimo Berroa led off the 10th inning with back-to-back homers off closer Jose Mesa to lift the Oakland Athletics to an 11-9 victory over the Cleveland Indians.
After Cleveland's Tony Fernandez doubled in Omar Vizquel in the bottom of the ninth to force extra innings, McGwire blasted his second homer of the game and 11th of the year to begin the 10th.

McGwire finished with three hits, three runs and three RBI, including a two-run homer in the fifth that travelled 485 feet, hitting the scoreboard in left field. It was the second-longest homer of his career.
Billy Taylor (1-1) earned the win despite allowing the tying run to score in the ninth.
In Detroit, Melvin Nieves drilled a three-run double to cap a four-run third inning as the Detroit Tigers snapped the Milwaukee Brewers' season-high four-game winning streak with an 8-4 victory.
Brian Hunter, who had three hits, started the third-inning rally with a one-out infield single.

In Minnesota, Brady Anderson drove in three runs and B.J. Surhoff had four hits, including his first home run of the season, as the Baltimore Orioles handed the Minnesota Twins their seventh straight loss, 12-3.

Minnesota tied the game in the fifth on Rich Becker's run-scoring single, but the Orioles took the lead for good in the sixth against starter Bob Tewksbury. Mike Bordick drew a two-out walk and scored on Anderson's triple into the right-centre field gap.

In Kansas City, Roger Clemens allowed three hits over eight innings to outduel Kevin Appier, and Carlos Delgado's second-inning homer accounted for all the scoring as the Toronto Blue Jays blanked the Kansas City Royals, 1-0.

Clemens (4-0) walked two and struck out seven. He has won four of his five starts this season and pitched at least seven innings in all but one. Paul Spoljaric recorded the final out for his first save.
"In tight ballgames its important to get one run and keep putting up zeros," Clemens said. "I was sitting back throwing a lot of pitches. But I'm built for that, I'm trained for that."
